kill_criterion: If the number of distinct length-128 prefixes saturates at some K0 <= 64 for all larger k that the data supports, the finite-kernel hypothesis survives the screen (then try to identify a 2-DFA; if you cannot, still report saturation). Finite kernel does NOT prove periodicity (Thue-Morse), so that is NOT a prize claim; it kills THIS route as a nonperiodicity proof unless you can still prove the identified automatic sequence is not eventually periodic AND equals c, which is a much stronger claim — do not claim it without a proof. If distinct prefixes grow like 2^k (full kernel) through k=12, the screen does not kill automaticity-of-small-kernel, but also does NOT prove infinite kernel. Optionally try a structural lemma (e.g. a family r_k where kernel words disagree at a predicted index using the CA). If no lemma, kill the proof-via-automaticity route.
